tutorial.title: Understanding Functions
tutorial.descriptionContent: Learn how to name functions and why you can think of them as black boxes.

lessons.title: Lesson #1
lessons.interactiveContent:
Function names should be descriptive and should indicate the main purpose of the function. This function shows something in the game HUD.

Make sure to pick display.

lessons.title: Lesson #2
lessons.interactiveContent:
Functions are actions, so their names should contain at least one verb. When using multiple words, the verb is a prefix, like addScore.

Make sure to pick add, followed by Score.

lessons.title: Lesson #3
lessons.interactiveContent:
Functions that mainly return a value without changing it in any way start with verbs like get.

Make sure to pick getPlayerName.

lessons.title: Lesson #4
lessons.interactiveContent:
As a special case, functions that return boolean values often start with is.

Make sure to pick isGameOver.

lessons.title: Lesson #5
lessons.interactiveContent:
Function names should be consistent. If one function is called calculateDamage, a similar function should have the same verb prefix.

Make sure to pick calculateHeal.

lessons.title: Lesson #6
lessons.interactiveContent:
Why do we give functions descriptive names?

So we can figure out what they do by the name aloneSo our game can run on a computer

So we can figure out what they do by the name alone.

lessons.title: Lesson #7
lessons.interactiveContent:
What's necessary for a function name to have?

A verbA noun

A verb.

lessons.title: Lesson #8
lessons.interactiveContent:
Where do we add the verb in a function name?

At the beginning, as a prefixAt the end, as a suffix

At the beginning, as a prefix.

lessons.title: Lesson #9
lessons.interactiveContent:
How do we name similar functions?

We stay consistent and use the same verbWe give all functions the exact same name

We stay consistent and use the same verb.

lessons.title: Lesson #10
lessons.interactiveContent:
Code the correct name and function call to display the player score, 992.

Make sure to pick displayPlayerScore, followed by displayPlayerScore.

lessons.title: Lesson #11
lessons.interactiveContent:
Code an appropriate function name for a function that returns a value.

Make sure to pick getFinalScore.

lessons.title: Lesson #12
lessons.interactiveContent:
As a special case, functions that return boolean values often start with is.

Make sure to pick isAtMaxHealth.

lessons.title: Lesson #13
lessons.interactiveContent:
Code the correct verb prefix for this function.

Make sure to type display.

lessons.title: Lesson #1
lessons.interactiveContent:
A function is like a black box because with a great name we can call a function without reading the code defined inside it.

Make sure to pick spawnPlayer(playerName);.

lessons.title: Lesson #2
lessons.interactiveContent:
For example, without reading the code defined inside the functions, can you guess what happens when this code runs?

A level name, a player name, and a high score display in the consoleHello, world displays in the console

A level name, a player name, and a high score display in the console.

lessons.title: Lesson #3
lessons.interactiveContent:
While we don't have to remember the code of every function in a program, we do have to pass the right input to get the right output.

Make sure to pick levelName, followed by startingLives.

lessons.title: Lesson #4
lessons.interactiveContent:
The right input depends on what types of values we pass to a function. Pass the string first, followed by the number.

Make sure to pick "Nova", followed by 350.

lessons.title: Lesson #5
lessons.interactiveContent:
The value types matter when functions perform operations. For example, when adding two numbers, the values we pass have to be numbers.

Make sure to pick 100, 50.

lessons.title: Lesson #6
lessons.interactiveContent:
A function's output doesn't have to be the same type as the input. This function has a number as input and a boolean as output.

Make sure to pick 25.

lessons.title: Lesson #7
lessons.interactiveContent:
When we think about a function's output, we can think about what it displays or what it returns to be used somewhere else in the code.

Make sure to pick return.

lessons.title: Lesson #8
lessons.interactiveContent:
Why are functions like black boxes?

Because we can use them without knowing the code inside themBecause we never know their input or output

Because we can use them without knowing the code inside them.

lessons.title: Lesson #9
lessons.interactiveContent:
What does this code display in the console?

It displays the current levelIt displays the current score

It displays the current level.

lessons.title: Lesson #10
lessons.interactiveContent:
How do we decide a function's input?

Based on the output we wantBased on how many values we have available

Based on the output we want.

lessons.title: Lesson #11
lessons.interactiveContent:
What happens when we pass the wrong type of value to a function?

The function won't work as intendedIt doesn't matter, the function still works

The function won't work as intended.

lessons.title: Lesson #12
lessons.interactiveContent:
What happens when we pass string values to this function instead of numbers?

We get the string "1025", and not the sum 35We get the sum of the two numbers, 35

We get the string "1025", and not the sum 35.

lessons.title: Lesson #13
lessons.interactiveContent:
What happens when a function's input is a different type than the output?

The function works, the input can be a different type compared to the outputIt won't work, input and output have to be the same type

The function works, the input can be a different type compared to the output.

lessons.title: Lesson #14
lessons.interactiveContent:
Which of these can be considered as output?

What a function displays in the console or what it returnsThe operations a function carries out

What a function displays in the console or what it returns.

lessons.title: Lesson #15
lessons.interactiveContent:
Code the right function name.

Make sure to pick spawnPlayer.

lessons.title: Lesson #16
lessons.interactiveContent:
Pass the right input to get the right output.

Make sure to pick playerName, followed by playerName, and finally levelName.

lessons.title: Lesson #17
lessons.interactiveContent:
Code the parameters so that their names match the order of the values passed.

Make sure to pick points, followed by name.

lessons.title: Lesson #18
lessons.interactiveContent:
Code the right values to get a number as output.

Make sure to pick 1300, 15.

lessons.title: Lesson #19
lessons.interactiveContent:
Display the boolean false in the console.

Make sure to pick "Slime".

lessons.title: Lesson #1
lessons.interactiveContent:
Let's learn about functions with arrays as parameters. Pass the enemies array to the displayEnemies() function to get started.

Make sure to pick displayEnemies followed by ( and then enemies, ), ;.

lessons.title: Lesson #2
lessons.interactiveContent:
When we pass arrays to functions we can choose among a number of results based on the array. For example, we can display the entire array.

Make sure to pick enemies.

lessons.title: Lesson #3
lessons.interactiveContent:
We could also display the length of the array. In this example, using enemies.length.

Make sure to pick enemies, followed by ., and finally length.

lessons.title: Lesson #4
lessons.interactiveContent:
A third example is using a single element of the array, for example by coding enemies[0].

Make sure to pick enemies followed by [ and then 0, ].

lessons.title: Lesson #5
lessons.interactiveContent:
Often times we pass an array to a function because we want to return a part of it.

Make sure to pick return, followed by enemies[0], and finally ;.

lessons.title: Lesson #6
lessons.interactiveContent:
We can use multiple elements from an array to return a certain kind of output we need for the next step in our code.

Make sure to pick return, followed by enemies[0] + " + " + enemies[1], and finally ;.

lessons.title: Lesson #7
lessons.interactiveContent:
What does this code display in the console?

The entire enemies arrayThe first value of the enemies array

The entire enemies array.

lessons.title: Lesson #8
lessons.interactiveContent:
What does this code display in the console?

The array length followed by the value DragonThe array length followed by the value Imp

The array length followed by the value Dragon.

lessons.title: Lesson #9
lessons.interactiveContent:
What output does this have?

The second value of the arrayThe first value of the array

The second value of the array.

lessons.title: Lesson #10
lessons.interactiveContent:
What does this code display in the console?

Ranger NovaNova Ranger

Ranger Nova.

lessons.title: Lesson #11
lessons.interactiveContent:
Code the value that displays the entire array.

Make sure to pick items.

lessons.title: Lesson #12
lessons.interactiveContent:
Display the length of the items array.

Make sure to pick items, followed by ., and finally length.

lessons.title: Lesson #13
lessons.interactiveContent:
Display the first array element.

Make sure to type sprites[0].

lessons.title: Lesson #14
lessons.interactiveContent:
Return the array's second element.

Make sure to pick return followed by levels and then [1], ;.

lessons.title: Lesson #15
lessons.interactiveContent:
Choose the right value type as input to make this function work.

Make sure to pick [10, 5, 8].
